slot_note: wave 5, third of six, re-rooted from architecture 1 (the transit nominations); the seed's world (ET25) dropped, the objective kept
niche: a regional health plan's specialty pharmacy clinical program, staffing its clinical pharmacists across drug classes by the spend each class's members already on therapy will run over the program year, from two pharmacy benefit managers' claim files
stakeholder_role: Director of Pharmacy, the plan's clinical pharmacy program

spine.entity: one pharmacy claim line (a fill, a reversal or a rebill) for a specialty drug
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a PBM's paid claims extract)
spine.row_meaning: a specialty fill, reversal or rebill as the outgoing PBM paid it

world.geography: United States, an unnamed state (the health plan, its PBMs, the drugs' product names and the people are fictional)

driver: The decisive quantity is what the units in each group that are active today will cost over the coming year, where cost and the chance of staying active both depend on how long a unit has been active, and the groups differ in how recently their active units started; carrying the latest run-rate or trailing year forward, applying last year's active units' following-year experience, or a group's persistence curve read from each unit's start all misstate the groups whose active units are newer or older than usual, and only each group's development conditional on time since start, applied to today's units at their own durations, gets the shares right.
driver_concrete: Each specialty class's spend over July 2026 to June 2027 on the members whose fill covers 30 June 2026 is built from the class's own month-by-month continuation and paid amount by months on therapy, read from every member who has passed each month since their first fill across both PBMs' files; the weight-loss class filled with new starters after its 2026 coverage change, so last year's cohort overstates it, oncology's current users have survived its early discontinuation, so a curve from first fill understates it, and hepatitis C's fixed courses end within weeks.
stump: The default path carries each class's trailing year, or its June run-rate, forward for the members on therapy and staffs the classes on those shares, so the hepatitis C, oncology and weight-loss classes take pharmacists their current users will not need; applying last year's on-therapy cohort's following-year spend per member still over-staffs the weight-loss class (its 2026 users are new and most will stop within months), and a persistence curve read from each member's first fill under-staffs oncology (today's users have already survived its early discontinuation); only each class's development by months on therapy, applied at each current member's own duration, gives the golden allocation.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms both PBMs' files (reversals netted, members linked across the PBM change, NDCs normalised, the 2026 prices applied) and reads every charter rule projects each class's current users by last year's on-therapy cohort's following-year spend per member and allocates the 24 pharmacists on those shares, giving the weight-loss class pharmacists that belong to oncology and the persistent classes; the projection by months on therapy at each member's own duration gives the golden allocation.
domain_test: Pharmacy benefit forecasting's own analysis decides: a specialty class's forward spend for the members on therapy is the class's persistence and cost by months on therapy (loading doses, fixed courses, early discontinuation) applied at each member's own duration; swapping the nouns (hospital wards, megawatt-hours) leaves no months on therapy, no loading dose and no fixed course, which are why the classes' current users differ from last year's.
layer1: two PBMs' claim files in different layouts (the outgoing PBM's reversals as negative lines, the incoming PBM's as a status column)
member identifiers re-keyed at the PBM change through a crosswalk
the incoming PBM's 2026 contract prices against the outgoing PBM's paid amounts
transition-of-care fills at the January 2026 PBM change

differentiation.task98: task98 v6 counts units under a score threshold whose closed periods were scored on a classifier the improvement programme could not move; here no classifier changes: the forward quantity is each group spend developed by how long its active units have been active, read from every unit that has passed each duration.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a per-unit count assembled from records that a matcher links to units, where the matcher fails far more often for some units' records, so the unlinked records are not distributed like the linked ones, and the review that measures their mix draws clusters at random and one record within each, so a cluster holding many unlinked records is seen no more often than one holding a single record; the review's raw mix, like a share-out in proportion to the linked records, understates the units whose clusters fail most, and only each reviewed record weighted by its cluster's count of unlinked records restores each unit's count.
lineage.niche: a city transit department's delivered-frequency evidence for a state capital program, built by linking vehicle-location departure records to routes through a vendor's trip matcher that leaves late-running departures unmatched, with the department's trip-matching review sample
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-19: four isolated readers landed the call (score_reader exit 1, Gate F) and judge pass 3 found the shelter ask NOT_DETERMINISTIC (the moved-stop rule unstated); re-rooted by the author's decision
